mainTopic: Which quality of land ניזקין, a בעל חוב and a כתובה are collected from, the reasons behind these rules, and מר זוטרא's limit on the כתובה rule
overview: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי עקיבא says the תורה's 'best of his field' means the best land of the מזיק. רבינא explains that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, and its words 'מפני תיקון העולם' only give the reason for the תורה law, the way רבי שמעון explains the reasons behind פסוקים. רבי שמעון's ברייתא gives those reasons. ניזקין collect from עידית so people won't rob. A בעל חוב collects from בינונית so people won't lend just to grab a nice field, but not from זיבורית, because then no one would lend. A כתובה is collected from זיבורית because a woman wants to marry more than a man does. His 'דבר אחר' explains why the husband gets no כתובה from his wife: divorce is always in the husband's hands. מר זוטרא then says the זיבורית rule for a כתובה applies only when collecting from orphans, and from the husband himself she gets בינונית. The גמרא defends him against challenges from רבא and אביי. To answer אביי, רב אחא בר יעקב sets the משנה in a case where a father was a קבלן for his son's debts. The amud ends with a teaching that everyone agrees a regular עָרֵב for a כתובה is not bound, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows how רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא read 'the best of his field'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא openly states the disagreement: רבי ישמעאל says the פסוק means the best land of the ניזק, and רבי עקיבא says it means the best land of the מזיק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught clearly in a ברייתא: 'Of the best of his field and the best of his vineyard he shall pay.' This means the best field and best vineyard of the injured person. That is רבי ישמעאל's view. רבי עקיבא says it means the best field and best vineyard of the one who did the damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says outright that, according to רבי עקיבא, the תורה is talking about the best land of the person who caused the damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'his field' in the פסוק could refer to either person. רבי ישמעאל says 'his' means the ניזק, so we compare to the victim's best land. רבי עקיבא says 'his' means the מזיק, so by תורה law the payment is measured by the damager's own best land, which makes the עידית rule a תורה law.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught explicitly (in a ברייתא)
The injured party, the one who suffered damage
The one who caused the damage

steps.confusionAlert: Both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא use the same words 'the best of his field'. They only disagree about whose field 'his' refers to.

phrases.english: It is taught explicitly in a baraita:
"Of the best of his field and the best of his vineyard he shall pay"
means the best of the field of the injured party,
and the best of the vineyard of the injured party;
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: מֵיטַב שָׂדֵהוּ שֶׁל מַזִּיק,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: the best of the field of the one who caused the damage,
and the best of the vineyard of the one who caused the damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא בְּהֶדְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an explicit ברייתא to support the earlier claim about רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי עקיבא, by תורה law we measure by the best land of the מזיק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the disagreement between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא on the פסוק 'מיטב שדהו ומיטב כרמו ישלם'.

steps.title: רבינא: the משנה follows both רבי עקיבא and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, and 'מפני תיקון העולם' is just רבי שמעון-style reasoning that explains why the תורה gave this law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Really, the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who says that by תורה law we look at the damager's land. It also follows רבי שמעון, who explains the reasons behind פסוקים. The משנה means: what is the reason that ניזקין collect from the best land? Because of תיקון העולם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא solves the problem: the משנה can follow רבי עקיבא, and the words 'מפני תיקון העולם' are only explaining the reason for the תורה's law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difficulty was that 'תיקון העולם' sounds like a rule the חכמים made up. But for רבי עקיבא the עידית rule is already a תורה law. רבינא says the משנה is not making a new rule. It is giving the reason for the תורה law, the way רבי שמעון likes to explain the reasons behind פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in truth (keeping the original position)
He explains the reason behind a פסוק
Improving society / keeping the world in good order

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'מפני תיקון העולם' does NOT mean the חכמים added a new rule. רבינא reads it as the reason for a rule that is already in the תורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the phrase תיקון העולם in a משנה can be the reason behind a תורה law, not only a sign of a rabbinic decree.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Actually, our mishna is according to Rabbi Akiva,
who said that by Torah law we appraise using the land of the one who caused damage;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא – דְּדָרֵישׁ טַעְמָא דִּקְרָא,
phrases.english: and it is also according to Rabbi Shimon, who expounds the reason of the verse,
and the mishna is saying 'what is the reason':

phrases.aramaic: מָה טַעַם הַנִּיזָּקִין שָׁמִין לָהֶן בְּעִידִּית?
phrases.english: What is the reason that for injured parties the court appraises from the best land?
For the betterment of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי עקיבא's view from the ברייתא and explains how the משנה's wording fits it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה's wording: 'מפני תיקון העולם' is a reason, not a new rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מפני תיקון העולם' seemed to show the עידית rule is rabbinic, which does not fit רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא, and like רבי שמעון it is giving the reason for the תורה law.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: ניזקין collect from the best land so people won't rob
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי שמעון explaining the reason for the עידית rule: it scares off robbers, because the court will take their nicest field.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא, רבי שמעון said: Why did they say ניזקין collect from the best land? Because of robbers and people who take things by force. A person will think: Why should I rob or take by force? Tomorrow בית דין will come to my property and take my nice field. And they rely on what the תורה says: 'Of the best of his field and the best of his vineyard he shall pay.' That is why they said ניזקין collect from the best land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רבינא's point by bringing a ברייתא where רבי שמעון gives the reason behind the תורה's עידית rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון says the rule protects society, because a would-be robber knows he will lose his best field. He ends by saying they rely on the פסוק, which shows the rule comes from the תורה and the 'reason' only explains it. This is exactly how רבינא read the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: People who take things by force, even if they pay for them
They go down to (seize) my property

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon said:
For what reason did they say
that for injured parties the court appraises from the best land?
Because of the robbers and because of those who take by force,
so that a person will say:

phrases.aramaic: לָמָה אֲנִי גּוֹזֵל וְלָמָה אֲנִי חוֹמֵס?
phrases.english: Why should I rob and why should I take by force?
Tomorrow the court will come down to my property
and take my nice field,
and they rely on what is written in the Torah:
"Of the best of his field and the best of his vineyard he shall pay";
phrases.notes: שמות 22:4, the same פסוק from the start.

phrases.english: therefore they said:
for injured parties the court appraises from the best land.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבינא's claim that רבי שמעון gives a 'reason' for the תורה's עידית rule.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון explains the עידית rule for ניזקין with a social reason while basing it on the פסוק.

steps.title: Why a creditor collects only from middle-quality land
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a בעל חוב collects from בינונית so people won't lend money just to grab someone's nice field or house.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they say a creditor collects from middle-quality land? So that a person will not see his friend's nice field and nice house and say: I will jump in and lend him money, so that I can collect it for my debt. That is why they said a creditor collects from middle-quality land.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון goes on and gives the reason for a second rule: a lender collects from average land, not the best land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If lenders could take the best land, someone might lend money hoping the borrower can't pay, just to grab his nice property. Limiting the lender to בינונית takes away that bad motive. It is a second example of רבי שמעון explaining the reason behind a rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A creditor, a lender who is owed money
I will jump in (rush to do something)

steps.whatToRemember: ניזקין collect from עידית so people won't steal; a בעל חוב collects from בינונית so people won't lend just to grab nice property. According to רבינא, תיקון העולם in the משנה is the reason for the תורה's law, following רבי עקיבא and רבי שמעון.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ בַּעַל חוֹב בְּבֵינוֹנִית?
phrases.english: For what reason did they say a creditor collects from middle-quality land?
So that a person should not see that his fellow has
a nice field and a nice house,
and say: I will jump in and lend him money,
so that I can collect it for my debt;
therefore they said: a creditor collects from middle-quality land.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ בַּעַל חוֹב בְּבֵינוֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא of רבי שמעון with the reason for the creditor's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל חוב collects from בינונית so people will not lend money just to seize someone's fine property.

steps.title: Then let the lender collect from the worst land
steps.stepSummary: If the goal is to stop people from lending just to grab good land, then a בעל חוב should collect from זיבורית.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that's the reason, let the lender collect from the worst land!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the reason just given for the בעל חוב rule. If we are worried that lenders want the borrower's good land, why not make them collect from the worst land?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said a lender collects from בינונית so that people won't lend just to grab a nice field. The גמרא takes that logic further: if the worry is the lender's greed for good land, giving him the worst land would remove that greed completely. So why stop at the middle level?

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if so (introduces a challenge that takes an idea to its logical end)

phrases.english: But if so, let it be from the worst land!
phrases.notes: "It" is the lender's collection from Step 4. If the worry is greed for nice fields, just give him the worst field.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, יְהֵא בְּזִיבּוּרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of Step 4 by taking it to its logical extreme.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason given for why a בעל חוב collects from בינונית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the worry is that lenders want good land, the worst land would solve it better than middle land.

steps.title: That would stop people from lending at all
steps.stepSummary: If lenders could only collect from the worst land, nobody would lend, and borrowers would be shut out.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, you would be locking the door in front of borrowers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Giving lenders only the worst land would make lending so unattractive that no one would lend money anymore.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule has to balance two concerns. Good land would invite greedy lending, and the worst land would kill lending completely. בינונית is the middle ground that keeps loans available without encouraging land-grabbing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This idea of 'not locking the door before borrowers' is a well-known reason the רבנן give in many places for protecting lenders.

phrases.english: If so —
you are locking the door in front of borrowers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן – אַתָּה נוֹעֵל דֶּלֶת בִּפְנֵי לוֹוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical consequence: the suggested rule would cause a worse problem.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Collecting from זיבורית would best prevent greedy lending.
steps.terutzMaskana: זיבורית would stop all lending, so בינונית is the balanced rule.

steps.title: Where a כתובה is collected from, and רבי שמעון's reason
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a כתובה is collected from זיבורית, and רבי מאיר says from בינונית. רבי שמעון explains the זיבורית rule: a woman wants to marry more than a man does.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman's כתובה is collected from the worst land; this is רבי יהודה's view. רבי מאיר says: from middle land. רבי שמעון said: Why did they say a כתובה is collected from the worst land? Because a woman wants to get married even more than a man wants to marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to a new case, the כתובה. It brings a disagreement about which land it is collected from, and רבי שמעון gives a reason for the זיבורית view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון explains the rule by looking at who needs the deal more. Since a woman is eager to marry, she will agree to marry even with a weaker guarantee. So the רבנן don't need to give her better land to make marriage happen.

keyTerms.meaning: To become married (said of the woman)

phrases.english: A woman's כתובה is collected from the worst land,
these are the words of רבי יהודה.
רבי מאיר says: from middle land.
רבי שמעון said:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ כְּתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה בְּזִיבּוּרִית?
phrases.english: Why did they say a woman's כתובה is from the worst land?
Because more than a man wants to marry,
a woman wants to be married.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה – בְּזִיבּוּרִית, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא continues from the נזקין and בעל חוב rules to the third category, a כתובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: a כתובה is collected from זיבורית. רבי מאיר: from בינונית. רבי שמעון's reason for זיבורית: the woman is more eager to marry, so she accepts a weaker guarantee.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's second statement: divorce depends on the husband
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון adds: a woman can be divorced with or without her consent, but a man divorces only when he wants to.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: a woman is sent out with her consent or against her will, but a man sends her out only when he wants to.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון adds a second line marked 'דבר אחר.' It points out that divorce is always in the husband's hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface this looks like a second reason for the זיבורית rule. But it doesn't clearly explain anything about land quality. That puzzle is what the גמרא will ask about next.

keyTerms.meaning: With her consent / by her will

phrases.english: Another explanation:
a woman is sent out with her consent or against her will,
but a man sends her out only when he wants to.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: אִשָּׁה יוֹצְאָה לִרְצוֹנָהּ וְשֶׁלֹּא לִרְצוֹנָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי שמעון adds a second statement after his first reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman can be divorced against her will, but a man divorces only if he chooses to.

steps.title: What is the 'other explanation' for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון's 'דבר אחר' is coming to explain.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'other explanation' about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the 'דבר אחר' is doing here. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason already explained the זיבורית rule, and the second line doesn't seem to say anything about land. So the גמרא wants to know what question this second line actually answers.

phrases.english: What is the 'other explanation'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דָּבָר אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of the second line in Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What question the 'דבר אחר' of רבי שמעון is answering.

steps.title: Why there is no כתובה for the husband
steps.stepSummary: The 'דבר אחר' answers why the רבנן didn't make the wife pay the husband a כתובה when she leaves. The answer is that she can never really leave on her own, because the husband can always hold back the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: just as when he divorces her the רבנן made him pay her a כתובה, so when she leaves, the רבנן should make her pay him a כתובה? Come and hear: a woman is sent out with or without her consent, but a man sends her out only when he wants. He can always keep her waiting for her גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the 'דבר אחר' is not about land at all. It answers a different question: why the כתובה only goes one way, from husband to wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think it would be fair for a wife who walks away to owe her husband a כתובה. But a divorce only happens when the husband agrees, since even if she pushes for it he can delay the גט. So in the end the divorce is always his choice, and he has no claim to a כתובה from her.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (brings up a possible question)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון gives the reasons behind all three collection rules: נזקין from עידית to scare off robbers, a בעל חוב from בינונית to balance lending, and a כתובה from זיבורית because the woman wants to marry. His 'דבר אחר' explains something else: the כתובה only goes from husband to wife, because divorce is always in the husband's hands.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the 'דבר אחר' as a second reason for זיבורית. The גמרא says it answers a different question: why there is no כתובה for the husband.

phrases.english: And if you would say,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּכִי מַפֵּיק לַהּ אִיהוּ –
phrases.english: just as when he sends her out —
the רבנן set up a כתובה for her from him;
so too when she leaves —
the רבנן should set up a כתובה for him from her?
Come and hear:
a woman is sent out with her consent or against her will,
but a man sends out only when he wants to —
he is able to keep her waiting for the גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, כִּי הֵיכִי דְּכִי מַפֵּיק לַהּ אִיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9 by showing what the 'דבר אחר' is meant to explain.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'דבר אחר' explains why there is no כתובה for the husband: divorce always depends on him, since he can delay the גט.

steps.title: מר זוטרא limits the זיבורית rule to orphans
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says the משנה's rule that a כתובה is collected from זיבורית applies only when she collects from the orphans. From the husband himself, she collects from בינונית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says a woman's כתובה is collected from the worst land. מר זוטרא, son of רב נחמן, said: we said this only when she collects from the orphans. But when she collects from the husband himself, she gets medium land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about the כתובה, and מר זוטרא says it only applies to one case: collecting from the orphans after the husband dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said כתובה comes from זיבורית without any limits. מר זוטרא narrows it: if the husband divorced her and is alive, she collects from בינונית. So the low-quality rule only kicks in when the heirs are paying.

keyTerms.meaning: The money a husband promises his wife, paid if he divorces her or dies
The worst-quality land in a person's property
Orphans; here, the husband's heirs after he dies
From him himself, meaning from the husband while he is alive

phrases.english: A woman's marriage contract is collected from the worst land.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Nachman, said:
We only said this when collecting from orphans,
phrases.notes: The orphans are the husband's heirs, so this is the case where he died.

phrases.english: but from the husband himself, it is from medium land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא מִיַּתְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's rule that a כתובה is collected from זיבורית (the same rule רבי יהודה states in the ברייתא of step 7) and limits its scope.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כתובה is collected from זיבורית only from orphans. From the husband himself it is collected from בינונית.

steps.title: If it means orphans, why mention the כתובה at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges מר זוטרא: every debt is collected from orphans only from זיבורית, so the משנה would not need to single out the כתובה. It must be talking about the husband himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: From orphans?! Why single out a woman's כתובה? Every kind of debt works that way, because we learned: we collect from orphans' property only from the worst land! So isn't the משנה talking about collecting from the husband himself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks מר זוטרא's reading of the משנה by asking why the כתובה would be singled out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is already a general rule that any debt collected from orphans comes only from זיבורית. If the משנה only meant orphans, saying 'כתובה' adds nothing new. So the משנה seems to mean the husband himself, which goes against מר זוטרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it...? (pushing toward the other option)

phrases.english: From orphans?!
Why specifically a woman's marriage contract?
Even all other debts work this way too,
for we learned:
We do not collect from the property of orphans
except from the worst land!
Rather, isn't it talking about collecting from him?
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the husband himself, while he is alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיַּתְמֵי?! מַאי אִירְיָא כְּתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges מר זוטרא's limiting of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's claim that the משנה's זיבורית rule is only about orphans
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since all debts from orphans already come from זיבורית, naming the כתובה would be pointless. So the משנה must mean the husband himself.

steps.title: The כתובה needed to be mentioned anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends מר זוטרא: it really is about orphans, but the כתובה needed to be said. We might have thought the רבנן were easier on her so women would want to marry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really it is talking about orphans, and the כתובה needed to be mentioned. You might have thought: to make women want to marry, the רבנן were easier on her and let her collect better land even from orphans. So the משנה teaches us that she doesn't.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what new thing the משנה teaches by naming the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We could have guessed the כתובה is an exception to the orphans rule, because the רבנן wanted marriage to be attractive to women. The משנה tells us no: even the כתובה is collected from orphans only from זיבורית. So mentioning it is not wasted, and מר זוטרא stands.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought to say
Appeal; making women want to marry
It teaches us (that this is not so)

phrases.english: Really, it is talking about orphans,
and the woman's marriage contract needed to be mentioned:
it could have entered your mind to say:
for the sake of appeal, the Rabbis were lenient with her;
phrases.notes: 'Lenient' here means letting her collect better land than the usual orphans rule allows.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that this is not so.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם מִיַּתְמֵי, וּכְתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 and keeps מר זוטרא's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the specific case was needed (צריכותא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן might have made an exception for the כתובה, letting her collect better land even from orphans, so women would want to marry.
steps.terutzMaskana: No exception: even a כתובה is collected from orphans only from זיבורית, so the משנה needed to say it.

steps.title: רבא brings רבי מאיר's opinion
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes רבי מאיר, who says a כתובה is collected from בינונית, and asks: from whom is she collecting?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: come and hear. רבי מאיר says: a woman's כתובה is collected from medium land. From whom is she collecting?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a source to test מר זוטרא, and opens with a question. This step sets up the argument that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר argues with the רבנן, who say זיבורית. To see what the רבנן mean, רבא first has to figure out what case רבי מאיר is talking about: orphans or the husband himself.

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
Rabbi Meir says:
A woman's marriage contract is collected from medium land.
From whom?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: תָּא שְׁמַע, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After מר זוטרא was defended, רבא brings a new source to test his view.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the רבנן say זיבורית even when collecting from the husband himself
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי מאיר: כתובה is collected from בינונית

steps.title: So the רבנן say זיבורית even from the husband
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר cannot mean orphans, since all agree orphans pay from זיבורית. So he means the husband, and the רבנן who argue must say זיבורית even from the husband, against מר זוטרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say she collects from orphans, does רבי מאיר not agree with what we learned, that we collect from orphans only from the worst land?! So he must mean from the husband himself. That shows the רבנן hold she collects from the worst land, even from the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his argument and shows that the רבנן disagree with מר זוטרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's בינונית can't be about orphans, because the general rule for orphans is זיבורית. So he is talking about the husband himself. Since the רבנן argue with him, they must say זיבורית even from the husband, which is exactly what מר זוטרא said is not so.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who argue with רבי מאיר

steps.whyThisMatters: This leaves מר זוטרא facing a challenge from the opinion of the רבנן themselves, so his view now needs a defense.

phrases.english: If you say she collects from orphans,
does Rabbi Meir not hold
that which we learned:
We do not collect from the property of orphans
except from the worst land?!
Rather, isn't it from him, the husband himself?
This shows that the Rabbis hold it is from the worst land!
phrases.notes: Meaning even when she collects from the husband himself, which goes against מר זוטרא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא מִיַּתְמֵי, לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר הָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'from whom?' question of step 14 and uses it to challenge מר זוטרא.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's claim that from the husband himself she collects from בינונית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר must be talking about the husband, since orphans always pay from זיבורית. So the רבנן who argue with him say זיבורית even from the husband.

steps.title: רבי מאיר may be talking about orphans after all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's proof. רבי מאיר could be talking about collecting from orphans. The כתובה is different because the רבנן wanted women to want to marry.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really he means collecting from the orphans, and a woman's כתובה is different because of desirability.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks רבא's proof against מר זוטרא. רבי מאיר's ruling of בינונית could really be about orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed that everyone agrees orphans always pay from זיבורית, so רבי מאיר must mean the husband. The גמרא says no: רבי מאיר may give the כתובה a special exception even from orphans, so that women will be eager to marry. If so, the רבנן who argue with him are also talking about orphans, and nothing here goes against מר זוטרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; used to hold on to the original reading
Because of desirability, so women will want to marry

phrases.english: No; really, it is from the orphans,
and a woman's כתובה is different
because of desirability.
phrases.notes: This is the same idea from step 13: make marriage attractive to women. Here רבי מאיר goes further and gives her בינונית even from orphans.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; לְעוֹלָם מִיַּתְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion of step 15 by reading רבי מאיר as talking about orphans.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's whole proof against מר זוטרא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא assumed no one ever gives better land when collecting from orphans. But רבי מאיר may make an exception for the כתובה because of חינא.

steps.title: אביי quotes the משנה's list of land qualities
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a new source, our משנה: damages are paid from עידית, a lender from בינונית, and a כתובה from זיבורית.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Come and hear. For people who were damaged, the court assesses payment from the best land. A lender is paid from middle land. A woman's כתובה is paid from the worst land.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new attack on מר זוטרא by quoting the משנה. This step only sets up the source; the challenge itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists three kinds of debts, each paid from a different quality of land. אביי will use the fact that the list treats the כתובה differently from the other two.

phrases.english: אביי said: Come and hear:
For injured parties, the court assesses payment from the best land,
and a creditor is paid from middle-quality land,
and a woman's כתובה is paid from the worst land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's proof was pushed off, אביי brings a fresh source against מר זוטרא.
steps.raayaObject: That a כתובה is paid from זיבורית even from the husband himself, against מר זוטרא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's three-level list: damages from עידית, lender from בינונית, כתובה from זיבורית.

steps.title: If it meant orphans, why single out the כתובה?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks whom the משנה is talking about. If it meant orphans, every debt would be paid from זיבורית, so it must mean the husband himself. That goes against מר זוטרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: From whom is she collecting? If you say from the orphans, why mention only a woman's כתובה? All of these others would also be paid from the worst land! So isn't it talking about the husband himself?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי turns the משנה into a challenge. The list only makes sense if it is talking about the husband himself, not about orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From orphans, every debt is paid from זיבורית. So if the משנה were about orphans, the damaged person and the lender would not get better land. Since the משנה gives them better land, it must be talking about the living debtor, and then the כתובה is זיבורית even from the husband, against מר זוטרא.

keyTerms.meaning: From him, meaning the husband himself

steps.confusionAlert: Step 12 asked a question that sounds very similar, but it was about one line of the משנה. Here אביי uses the whole list. The damages and loan rows prove the משנה is talking about a living debtor, because orphans would never pay them from better land.

phrases.english: From whom?
If you say from the orphans,
why mention specifically a woman's כתובה?
Even all of these too would be paid from the worst land!
phrases.notes: "All of these" means the damaged person and the lender. From orphans, they too would get only זיבורית.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not from him himself?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאן? אִילֵימָא מִיַּתְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the משנה quoted in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's claim that from the husband himself a כתובה is paid from בינונית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives damages and loans better land, so it cannot be about orphans. It must be about the living debtor, and there it still says זיבורית for the כתובה.

steps.title: The father was a guarantor for his son
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב answers that the משנה is about a father who became an ערב for his son's damages, his son's loan, and his daughter-in-law's כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: What case are we dealing with here? A case where a man became a guarantor for his son's damages, for his son's creditor, and for his daughter-in-law's כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב defends מר זוטרא by explaining the משנה as a special case: a father guaranteed all of his son's debts. The next step explains why this answers אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed only two choices: the husband himself, or the orphans. רב אחא offers a third: a guarantor who pays in place of the son. In this case one person pays all three debts, but each debt can still follow its own rule.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? Used to set the משנה in a specific case
A guarantor, someone who promises to pay another person's debt

phrases.english: רב אחא בר יעקב said:
With what case are we dealing here?
For example, where he became a guarantor for his son's damages,
for his son's creditor,
and for his daughter-in-law's כתובה;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by setting the משנה in a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-setting the case (הכא במאי עסקינן): the משנה is about a guarantor, not the husband or the orphans.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought the משנה had to be about the husband himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a father who guaranteed his son's debts, so it says nothing about a husband paying his own כתובה.

steps.title: Each debt follows its own rule
steps.stepSummary: The guarantor pays each debt the way it would normally be paid. Damages and loans are paid as if the son were alive. The כתובה is paid as if it came from orphans, so from זיבורית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Each one follows its own law. Damages and loans are normally collected while the debtor is alive, so the guarantor also pays as though the son were alive. A כתובה is normally collected after death, and after death from whom does she collect? From orphans. So the guarantor also pays as though it were after death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב אחא's answer by explaining why the guarantor pays different debts from different land. This explains the whole משנה without contradicting מר זוטרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Damages and loans are normally collected from a living person, so they get עידית and בינונית. A כתובה is normally collected after the husband dies, from orphans, so the guarantor pays like orphans, from זיבורית. The משנה's זיבורית for the כתובה is really the orphans' rule, just as מר זוטרא said.

keyTerms.meaning: During life, while the debtor is alive
He pays out (the debt is collected through him)

steps.whatToRemember: מר זוטרא survives both attacks. רבי מאיר's בינונית can be a special favor for the כתובה, even from orphans. The משנה's זיבורית can be about a guarantor who pays the כתובה the way orphans would. So a husband paying his own כתובה can still pay from בינונית.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea: a guarantor steps into the shoes of the debt. He pays at the level the debt would normally be paid, not at a level based on who he is.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי כִּי דִינֵיהּ, וְהַאי כִּי דִינֵיהּ;
phrases.english: And this one follows its law, and that one follows its law;
injured parties and creditors, who collect during the debtor's lifetime,

phrases.aramaic: אִיהוּ נָמֵי כִּי מַגְבֵּי – כְּמֵחַיִּים מַגְבֵּי.
phrases.english: when he too pays them, he pays as though during life.
phrases.notes: "He" is the father, the guarantor. He pays as if the son were still alive, so they get עידית and בינונית.

phrases.english: A woman's כתובה, which she collects after death,
and after death, from whom does she collect? From the orphans;

phrases.aramaic: אִיהוּ נָמֵי כִּי מַגְבֵּי – כִּלְאַחַר מִיתָה מַגְבֵּי.
phrases.english: so when he too pays it, he pays as though after death.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי כִּי דִינֵיהּ, וְהַאי כִּי דִינֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב אחא's guarantor case in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the guarantor case: each debt is paid at its normal level.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed odd that one guarantor would pay three debts from three different kinds of land.
steps.terutzMaskana: The guarantor copies the normal way each debt is collected. The כתובה is normally collected from orphans, so it is paid from זיבורית, which fits מר זוטרא.

steps.title: A guarantor of a כתובה is not bound at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אחא בר יעקב's case. A guarantor for a כתובה is normally not bound to pay, so the father should not owe anything for the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him get it from the rule that a guarantor of a כתובה is not bound to pay!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 19. If the father is only a guarantor for the כתובה, there is a known rule that such a guarantor does not have to pay at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא בר יעקב said the משנה is about a father who guaranteed his daughter-in-law's כתובה. But the rule is that a guarantor of a כתובה is not truly bound. So why would the משנה need the 'orphans' reasoning for the כתובה, when the father should owe nothing?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him get it from a different reason instead
A guarantor, someone who backs another person's debt
Becomes bound, legally obligated to pay

phrases.english: But let him derive it instead
from the rule that a guarantor of a כתובה does not become bound!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּעָרֵב דִּכְתוּבָּה לֹא מִשְׁתַּעְבֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the guarantor case set up in Steps 19-20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's reading that the משנה is about a father who guaranteed his son's obligations, including the כתובה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A guarantor of a כתובה is not bound at all, so the father should not pay the כתובה, and the case does not fit the משנה.

steps.title: The father was a full-responsibility guarantor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the father was a קבלן, a guarantor who takes on full responsibility, so he is bound even for a כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a קבלן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in one word: the father was a קבלן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular guarantor of a כתובה is not bound. A קבלן is a stronger kind of guarantor who accepts the debt directly, so the woman can collect from him. That makes the father truly bound, and the case of the משנה works again.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantor who accepts full, direct responsibility for the debt

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up a regular עָרֵב with a קבלן. The rule 'a guarantor of a כתובה is not bound' is about the regular kind; a קבלן is bound.

phrases.english: It is dealing with an unconditional guarantor.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּקַבְּלָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a specific type of guarantor.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father was a regular guarantor, who is not bound for a כתובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father was a קבלן, who is bound even for a כתובה.

steps.title: What about the opinion that a קבלן needs the borrower to have property?
steps.stepSummary: The answer works for the view that a קבלן is always bound. But for the view that a קבלן is bound only if the borrower had property, what do we say?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is fine for the one who says a קבלן is bound even if the borrower has no property. But for the one who says he is bound only if the borrower has property, and not if he has none, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes on the קבלן answer. There is a disagreement about when a קבלן is bound, and the answer seems to work only for one side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One opinion: a קבלן is bound even when the borrower owns nothing. The other opinion: a קבלן is bound only if the borrower had property of his own. Under the second view, if the son owned nothing, the father never became bound, so the answer from Step 22 fails.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out fine (for one opinion)
According to the one who says
What is there to say? (a challenge)

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says: an unconditional guarantor,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵית לֵיהּ נִכְסֵי לְלֹוֶה
phrases.english: even though the borrower has no property,
is bound — then it is fine;
but according to the one who says:
if the borrower has property, the guarantor is bound,
if he does not have, he is not bound,
what is there to say?
phrases.notes: He means: if the son owned nothing, the father never became bound, so how does the case work?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the קבלן answer of Step 22 based on a dispute about when a קבלן is bound.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the father was a קבלן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the view that a קבלן is bound only when the borrower has property, a son with no property leaves the father unbound.

steps.title: The son had property that was later ruined
steps.stepSummary: First answer: the son did have property at the start, so the father became bound, but the property was later blighted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: it is where he had property and it got blighted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer. The son owned property at the beginning, so even the stricter opinion agrees the father became bound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the second opinion, what matters is that the borrower had property when the debt started. Here the son did, so the father became a bound קבלן. Later the land was ruined, so the woman now collects from the father.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces one possible answer)

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
it is where he had property and it was blighted.
phrases.notes: "He" is the son. His fields got ruined after the father had already become bound.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: בְּדַהֲווֹ לֵיהּ וְאִישְׁתְּדוּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23 by narrowing the case further.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case so it works even for the stricter opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The son never had property, so the father never became bound.
steps.terutzMaskana: The son had property at first, so the father became bound, and the property was ruined later.

steps.title: A father fully binds himself for his son
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: when it comes to his son, a father binds himself completely, even if the son has no property.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: in anything to do with his son, a father fully binds himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer. A father is different from a normal guarantor, because he is willing to commit himself fully for his son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stricter opinion assumes a קבלן does not truly mean to take on a debt when the borrower owns nothing. But a father, out of love for his son, does mean it. So even if the son had nothing, the father is bound, and רב אחא בר יעקב's case stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The father in the משנה was a קבלן. He is bound either because the son had property that was later ruined, or because a father fully commits himself for his son no matter what.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
with regard to anything relating to his son,
he truly binds himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: כֹּל לְגַבֵּי בְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical distinction about a father's intent toward his son.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A father is like any קבלן, not bound when the son owns nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: A father fully binds himself for his son, so he is bound even when the son owns nothing.

steps.title: Everyone agrees a guarantor for a marriage contract is not bound
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a stated teaching: all opinions agree that a regular עָרֵב who guarantees a כתובה does not become obligated to pay it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: a guarantor for a כתובה — all agree he is not bound to pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new statement about a guarantor for a כתובה, the topic that came up in the last few steps. This line sets up the next move, where opinions will split over a קבלן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 21-25 assumed that a regular guarantor for a כתובה is not bound. Now the גמרא states this openly as a rule that דברי הכל accept. Because everyone agrees here, the coming argument will be only about a קבלן, the stronger kind of guarantor.

keyTerms.meaning: A guarantor who promises to pay if the main person does not
Marriage contract: the husband's promise of money to his wife
Everyone agrees: no opinion argues on this point
Becomes bound or obligated, with his property held for the debt

steps.confusionAlert: This rule is only about a regular עָרֵב. A קבלן, who takes on full responsibility, is a separate case, and that is where the argument will be.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shared starting point explains why, back in step 22, the גמרא had to say the father was a קבלן and not just a regular guarantor.

phrases.english: It was stated: a guarantor for a marriage contract —
all agree he does not become obligated;

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: עָרֵב דִּכְתוּבָּה – דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל לָא מִשְׁתַּעְבַּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new teaching on the guarantor rule that steps 21-25 assumed while discussing רב אחא בר יעקב's case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A regular guarantor for a כתובה is not bound to pay it, and every opinion agrees.
